Review README.md and `/src` to replace the placeholder overview with the repository’s purpose and structure.

.NET 10 (`net10.0`), latest C#, nullable and implicit usings enabled; warnings are errors. Projects inherit settings from `Directory.Build.props`. Central package management is enabled: versions go in `Directory.Packages.props`; project package references omit versions. Add packages with `<PackageVersion Include="PackageName" Version="x.y.z" />`. XML warning 1591 is suppressed.

Use file-scoped namespaces, `_camelCase` private fields, PascalCase constants, `var` where appropriate, `I`-prefixed interfaces, and `Async` method suffixes. Use 2-space indentation, CRLF, UTF-8 BOM, Allman braces; prefer primary constructors (ALWAYS assign to readonly fields), top-level statements, pattern matching, and expression-bodied properties/indexers/accessors (NOT methods). Always use `{}` except single-line exits. Run `dotnet format`; analyzers are in `Directory.Build.props`.

Configuration: `appsettings.json`, environment overrides, `IConfiguration`/`IOptions<T>`, typed settings; User Secrets for development. Never hardcode sensitive information in source code. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging`, appropriate levels and context, structured logging where possible; avoid logging sensitive information; use correlation IDs when possible.

Use `Ardalis.GuardClauses` for non-UI validation and prefer `FluentValidation` for complex/UI validation. UI invalid inputs get friendly errors; non-UI invalid inputs throw appropriate guard-clause exceptions. HTTP methods return suitable failure status codes. Follow OWASP; validate/sanitize inputs, prevent SQL injection with parameterized queries/ORM, implement authentication/authorization, and use HTTPS.

Write unit-testable code; offer tests for generated code when applicable, in `tests/`. Only test controlled code with business logic, not framework code. Keep classes focused; use DI, composition, async/await for I/O, short methods (ideally under 20 lines), and short argument lists (consider parameter objects above 4).

Prefer FastEndpoints REPR and DDD where applicable. API messages use `*Request`/`*Response`; use cases `*Command`/`*Query`; use DTOs between layers, not exposed domain entities; DTOs may use `*Details`/`*Summary`. Avoid colocating interfaces and implementations.

Production projects: `src/`; tests: `tests/`, using xUnit. Run: `dotnet run --project src/YourProject/YourProject.csproj`

Use xUnit, Arrange-Act-Assert (whitespace only, no comments), feature-mirrored test folders, separate unit/integration tests. Do not name test classes with "Tests" suffix; do use "Tests" suffix for folder names if needed. Name classes `ClassName_MethodName.cs`, methods `DoesSomething_GivenSomeCondition`; together, names form a sentence. Use `[Fact]` or `[Theory]` with `[InlineData]`; prefer NSubstitute and Shouldly; avoid commercially licensed testing libraries (e.g. FluentAssertions, Moq).

Use Markdown documentation with headings, syntax-highlighted snippets, linting, and blank lines around lists/code listings. See `.editorconfig`, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, and `.gitignore`.
